verdict.pair_reasons:
X vs Y — X. Both hit all 20 key items and both ran a real, mostly-accurate stale-citation audit, so the decider is coverage depth and citation hygiene. Y explicitly did not read scripts/wrap-ledger.sh ("I did not read how wrap-ledger.sh computes RUNG, TRUNK, AHEAD or SHAS"), which the brief's "follow every library, helper and sibling file they source or shell out to" directly asks for; X read it and got three verified, material facts out of it that Y structurally could not have: BLOCKED>0 outranks 🔧 at :1971-1973 so a pending ⛔ decision suppresses the mechanical arm; 📦 still covers the "Land IN FLIGHT" readout at :1985-1986 and ship_floor reads only RUNG, so it can block mid-land; 🚀 requires LIVE_BREACH=1 at :2053-2056. X also carries four more verified extras Y lacks (the sibling Stop DELETING the armed sentinel at :1246-1251; the legacy mailbox_take fallback consuming `.seen` before emit at :1296-1297 via mailbox-pending.sh:370-380; window_end called with max 0 = uncapped at :1293; the KITTY_WINDOW_ID fallback-chain divergence between :420 and session-register.sh:134, which I reproduced). Against that Y has two outright wrong citations X does not (KILL_RE at :349 — it is :348; mailbox-drain.sh:224 called a mailbox_take_n call — it is `fi`, the call is :226) plus two truncated agent-identity.sh function ranges, while X's only real defect is one incomplete claim (RUNG=🔧 stated as DIRTY only, omitting REMAINDER at :1981-1982 and the six lower 🔧 arms). Y's unique win — the fully-verified demolition of :545-547's lead-crash-watchdog citation (classify_death is :402 not :255-278, marker_owns_sid is :207-213 not :112-118, and "verbatim" is false because the watchdog also requires "mode":"teardown" at :258) — is genuinely excellent, but it is one finding against X's six.

X vs Z — X. Z contradicts key item k10's precision note: it calls the wake floor's third disjunct "attributable open dispatched work" and says unattributable rows are merely worded as a hedge, when :758 sums cust_mine + cust_unk into the :805 predicate and :762-764 falls back to a bare cwd count; X states `cust = mine + unknown` explicitly and correctly. Z also makes a verified-false claim that its own text refutes — "Only arm whose jq -nc call sets both decision:\"block\" and systemMessage together (:892-893)" — when :1332 does precisely that on the armed path whenever mail was folded, which Z itself describes in Q4. Z's Q2 "additionally print" is wrong for the same structural reason (a wake-floor abstain returns 0, so its systemMessage replaces a block rather than accompanying one). Z partially misses k3 (never notes that a fresh `set` zeroes `.count`, the reason a compliant re-arming chain never caps) and k14 (names agent_assignee_argv but not the three-flag-plus-cross-field-consistency ancestry conjunction). Z's real wins — the sharper 🔧 ladder reading, and the genuinely unique observation that the mail fold sits below the kill-switch and CAP exits so neither surfaces mail — do not offset a contradicted key item plus a false "only" claim, and Z's stale-citation compliance is thin by its own admission (two items verified, the rest declined).

Y vs Z — Y. Y states k10 exactly as the key's precision note requires ("cust = mine + unknown (:758). Unattributable rows, possibly a sibling's, can therefore keep the floor re-firing, and the message says so (:881-882)"), where Z states it backwards; Y also gets the `set`-zeroes-the-counter half of k3 that Z omits. Z carries a verified-false material claim (the ":892-893 only arm" line, refuted by :1332) that Y has no counterpart to — Y's defects are small position errors (:349 for :348, :224's content) rather than false statements about behaviour. On the brief's explicit stale-citation instruction Y did the deeper, fully-verifiable job (five stale sites, each of which I confirmed) against Z's two-item check plus an honest decline. Z's fold-after-cap insight and its more precise wrap-ledger ladder reading are real and Y has neither, which keeps the margin modest rather than wide.
